_proposal.status: PROPOSED — NOT APPLIED. backtest/holdout_manifest.json is a sacred-harness file (CLAUDE.md 'Core principles'); this file stages the three Phase 4.F rows for human review and is never read by the harness.
_proposal.how_to_apply: Merge the three key/value pairs under 'entries' into the top-level object of backtest/holdout_manifest.json. Do NOT copy this '_proposal' key — holdout_manifest.json has no underscore-prefixed keys and every top-level key there is a strategy_id.
_proposal.shape_choice: The manifest schema (backtest/holdout.py _MANIFEST_SUBSTRATE_FIELDS) admits exactly one of 'symbol' | 'symbols' | 'legs' per entry, and none of the three can express a DYNAMIC universe (listings/delistings inside the window). Per the CC-2 work order these entries therefore use the single-'symbol' shape with symbol='BTCUSDT' as the DEV/HOLDOUT BOUNDARY ANCHOR only, and carry the real universe by reference in notes ('universe_ref'). Field set and ordering match the existing 9-key single-symbol entries (e.g. CrossSectionalMomentum) exactly: timeframe, data_start, data_end, dev_end, holdout_start, symbol, strategy_warmup_candles, min_tradeable_candles_per_block, notes.
open_questions_for_the_human: backtest/holdout.py:_load_substrate_df branches on whether the manifest symbol contains '/': a symbol WITHOUT a slash routes to load_binance_vision_signal_frame (the Binance Vision SPOT 1m substrate), not to data/binance_vision_um.py. 'BTCUSDT' as written would take that branch. Either the loader needs a binance_um branch (schema-stable code change, needs approval) or these rows need a different anchor convention. Flagged, not decided.

Timestamps use the '+00:00' offset form that every existing entry uses; the work order wrote dev_end/holdout_start as '2025-05-01T00:00:00Z', which is the same instant in a different spelling. Pick one before pasting.

The 5-minute 'metrics' archive (open interest) starts 2020-09-01, so DeleveragingReversal has no OI for the first ~8 months of its declared data_start. Either narrow its data_start to 2020-09-01 or accept the ragged start.
